title: Binary Search
intuition: Halves the remaining search window in every comparison by testing the midpoint of a sorted array.
whyExists: Provides logarithmic $O(\log n)$ lookup time on sorted datasets, reducing a billion elements to at most 30 comparisons.
analogy: Looking up a word in a printed physical dictionary: you flip open to the middle, check the letter, and discard the unneeded half.
coreIdea: Maintains boundaries low and high. Evaluates mid = low + (high - low) / 2. If a[mid] == target, search succeeds. If a[mid] < target, target must reside in right half, so low = mid + 1. Otherwise, high = mid - 1.

complexity.reason: Search space n is halved at each step: n / 2^k = 1 => k = log2(n).

pitfalls: Running binary search on an unsorted array produces incorrect results silently.
Integer overflow bug in midpoint: (low + high) / 2 can overflow for large indices. Always use low + (high - low) / 2.
Loop boundary conditions: using low < high instead of low <= high can miss the target when one element remains.
